# A US dollar card owing nothing, charged 150.00 USD and refunded 100.00 USD
# in one transaction at 1.40, the charge written first.
#
# a_usd_card_refunded_and_charged_in_one_transaction.txt writes the same two
# splits the other way round. GnuCash does not keep a transaction's splits in
# the order a file writes them, so what each split brought in across zero is
# read in an order of the import's own: the splits moving the account the way
# it moves overall come first. The card ends owing 50.00, so the charge is
# read first either way — it opens 150.00 owed, the refund repays 100.00 of
# it — and neither split crosses zero. The refund repays what the charge
# borrowed, so it states the charge's position as the cost basis it draws on
# (Q-050).
#
# Imported into the book usd_moved_out_of_an_empty_account.txt makes.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_balance_past_zero_has_a_cost_basis_on_the_other_side.py.
2034-02-01 * "Charged 150.00 USD and refunded 100.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Liabilities:USD Card -150.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "7/5"
		value: "-210.00"
	Liabilities:USD Card 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "7/5"
		value: "140.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: $transactions_to_import[0].splits[0].guid$
	Expenses:Travel 70.00 CAD
